config.title: AbortController & Cleanup in useEffect

intro.title: AbortController & Cleanup in useEffect
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React component that fetches and displays user data from a mock API, learning how to prevent memory leaks and unnecessary network requests. You will use the AbortController API to cancel a fetch request when a component unmounts or before a new request starts. The core programming concept is the cleanup function within the useEffect hook, which runs before the component re-renders or unmounts. You'll implement this in TypeScript to ensure type safety for the data you receive. By the end, you'll understand how to properly clean up side effects to create more efficient and reliable React applications.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential in any React application where data fetching is tied to user interactions that can change rapidly. For example, in a live dashboard with search filters, selecting a new filter triggers a new API call; using AbortController prevents the previous, now irrelevant request from updating the state if it completes later, avoiding race conditions and incorrect data displays. Similarly, in an e-commerce product listing, as a user types in a search bar, each keystroke might fetch suggestions, and aborting outdated requests ensures the UI shows only the latest results. Implementing cleanup in useEffect ensures these cancellations happen automatically when the component unmounts or dependencies change, preventing memory leaks and improving application stability.

objectives: Initialize an AbortController instance within a useEffect hook
Configure fetch requests to use the AbortController signal for cancellation
Implement cleanup logic in useEffect to abort pending requests on component unmount
Apply TypeScript typing to AbortController and signal properties
Construct a React component that safely fetches data with automatic cleanup
Manipulate component state only when fetch requests complete successfully
Integrate AbortController cleanup with multiple useEffect dependencies

steps.title: Implement useEffect with cleanup
steps.instruction: Add a useEffect hook inside your DataFetcher component that calls fetchData and returns a cleanup function that aborts the controller. The effect should run only once on mount.
steps.hint: The useEffect hook should be placed inside the component, after state declarations. The cleanup function should call abort() on the AbortController instance.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook is implemented with proper cleanup that aborts the fetch request when the component unmounts.
